103_question: Would the combination of known therapeutic delivery + spatial separation + retention + controlled residence have been obvious to a PHOSITA?

analysis.known_elements: Therapeutic delivery via shunt (CereVasc US11850390B2), drug retention (various), CSF drainage (standard)
analysis.novel_combination: Controlled separation between therapeutic introduction and the dominant CSF-clearance path in an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt
analysis.motivation_evidence: 11 passages teach drug delivery via shunt. 0 passages teach spatial separation of delivery from drainage. No motivation found for the COMBINATION.
analysis.expectation_of_success: A PHOSITA would not necessarily expect that spatial separation creates a material PK advantage. The eShunt's short length (80mm) and high drainage rate (1.4 mL/min) suggest the separation effect would be minimal — but the model shows it is not (327%).
analysis.teaching_away: The rapid CSF turnover (~7h) might teach AWAY from attempting drug residence in the shunt, as the conventional wisdom is that CSF drugs are quickly cleared.
analysis.unexpected_result: The 327% improvement IS unexpected because the shunt length is short relative to the drug distribution distance. The spatial separation effect is larger than a PHOSITA would predict.
analysis.conclusion: 103 leans NON_OBVIOUS but remains UNCERTAIN. The unexpected magnitude of the spatial separation effect (327% vs expected ~10-20%) supports non-obviousness. Patent counsel opinion required.
